title: Your business got a one-star from 'Craig.' A guy at the counter offers twenty fake five-stars for C$40.

outcomes.text: 'Sorry to hear it, Craig. Come back, the next one's on us.' You type it through gritted teeth.

later.text: Remember your polite reply to Craig's one-star? He came back, had a great time and changed it to four stars. 'Would have been five but Craig.'

outcomes.text: Twenty reviews appear overnight from accounts like 'GoodFood_Man_8.' Craig is buried. You're a 4.9 now.

later.text: Remember the twenty five-stars for C$40? The review site slapped a 'suspicious activity' banner on your page. Craig screenshotted it.

options.label: Ask regulars for honest ones
options.riskWhy: Some regulars are honest about you

outcomes.text: You ask your regulars. Eight post. Six are glowing, one says 'fine,' one is about the cat. It's real, and it shows.

title: Slow week at your business. Luis's tip jar has C$85. 'Borrowing' it would cover the ice order.

outcomes.text: You pay the ice guy from your own wallet. Luis never knows. That's the point.
You empty the jar into the ice order and leave a sticky note: 'IOU, the boss.' Very official.

later.text: Remember 'borrowing' Luis's tip jar for ice? He found the sticky note, quit, and now works across the street telling every customer why.

outcomes.text: You cover the ice and slip a twenty in Luis's jar. He notices and pretends not to, which is the classiest thing in Queens.

later.text: Remember the twenty in Luis's jar during the slow week? He's been bringing his whole soccer league in after games.

title: A regular hands you C$100 'for the lovely lady who folds my shirts.' Grace is off today.

outcomes.text: You put it in an envelope with 'From Mr. Ferreira, for the shirts.' Grace calls it the nicest Tuesday of her year.
'He left you fifty.' Grace is thrilled. You are fifty dollars thrilled, quietly.

later.text: Remember giving Grace half of Mr. Ferreira's C$100? He asked her if she liked 'the hundred.' She liked fifty of it. She told everyone.

outcomes.text: C$100 into the register. Mr. Ferreira waves goodbye. You wave back with his money.

later.text: Remember keeping Mr. Ferreira's C$100 for Grace? He thanked her for it. She asked you. You didn't have a good answer.

title: The vent filter at your business is due. C$180 now, or 'next month' like last month.

options.label: Fix it now
options.get: A clean vent, a clear head

outcomes.text: The vent guy pulls out a filter that looks like a wet raccoon. C$180. You sleep better.

later.text: Remember fixing the vent filter on time? Captain Rosa did a walk-through and called your place 'the cleanest on the block.' She posted it.

outcomes.text: Next month. The filter makes a sound like a disappointed parent.
Next month, again. You tape a 'do not look' sign on the vent.

later.text: Remember putting off the vent filter? It smoked out the lunch rush. Captain Rosa smelled it from Engine 7. Rush repair: C$250 and a lecture.

options.label: Fix it and post about it
options.get: A clean vent and some clout
options.riskWhy: Bragging about a vent is a choice

outcomes.text: 'Proud to announce our vent is clean 🙏.' It gets 300 likes and one comment: 'who is this for.' It's for you.

title: The fire extinguisher at your business expired in 2024. A new one is C$90. Nobody ever checks.

outcomes.text: New extinguisher, shiny and red. You keep looking at it like it's art. It is, kind of.

options.label: Peel the date off
options.cost: A small lie on a red can

outcomes.text: You peel off the date. The extinguisher looks fine. It's not fine. It's from 2024.

later.text: Remember peeling the date off your extinguisher? Captain Rosa stopped in for coffee and checked it out of habit. C$90 now, plus a stern look.

options.label: Ask Engine 7 for advice
options.cost: An afternoon and a box of pastries

outcomes.text: Captain Rosa takes the pastries and gives you the name of a guy who refills them for C$40. Hydrant gets a croissant.

title: Sudden downpour on Steinway. Your business has a box of umbrellas. They usually go for C$8.

outcomes.text: Ten umbrellas, ten soaked neighbors saved. One of them kisses the umbrella. C$80.
C$25 each. They sell out in four minutes. The tenth buyer says 'wow' in a voice that's not a compliment.

later.text: Remember the C$25 umbrellas in the rain? Lola posted 'Steinway's umbrella situation 👀' with a photo of your sign. Comments are wet and angry.

options.label: Give them to regulars, free
options.riskWhy: You might never see them again

outcomes.text: You hand out umbrellas to every regular who runs past. 'Bring it back whenever.' Some of them will. Some of them.

later.text: Remember the free umbrellas in the rain? Seven came back, each with a thank-you. One came back with a whole family who now shops only with you.

title: 92 degrees and a Meteors game just let out. Your business has the only cold water for blocks.

options.label: Keep it at C$2
options.get: C$120 and a lot of thank-yous

outcomes.text: Sixty bottles, C$2 each, sixty grateful fans in orange. One tells you the Meteors lost. You knew.

options.label: Make it C$6
options.riskWhy: Sports fans hold grudges for decades

outcomes.text: C$6 a bottle. They pay, sweating and furious. You make C$360 and a few enemies in foam fingers.

later.text: Remember the C$6 water after the Meteors game? A fan's photo of your sign is the top post in the team's fan forum. Section 7 has opinions.

options.label: Free cooler for anyone dizzy
options.riskWhy: Everyone will claim to be dizzy

outcomes.text: You put out a cooler: 'Free if you're dizzy.' Everyone is suddenly dizzy. You let them be dizzy.
